task.title: Stable range and multiselection
task.specification: config={options:[{id,disabled:boolean}]} unique IDs; initially selected=[],anchor=null. view={type:'view',options:[...]} replaces ordered options, drops selected IDs absent or disabled, and clears an absent/disabled anchor. click={type:'click',id,shift:boolean,ctrl:boolean} ignores absent/disabled IDs. A plain click replaces selection with id and sets anchor=id. Ctrl without Shift toggles id and sets anchor=id. Shift uses the current valid anchor, or establishes clicked id as anchor if absent; select the inclusive range in the CURRENT view between anchor and id, skipping disabled options. Ctrl+Shift unions that range with existing selection; Shift alone replaces selection. A Shift operation preserves an existing anchor. Output {selected:[lexicographically sorted IDs],anchor:ID|null}. Selection cannot retain filtered-out IDs under this explicit policy. Return one output per event. State is opaque JSON, initially null. Output objects have exactly the documented keys; object key order is irrelevant, array order is significant. IDs are nonempty ASCII strings. Values are JSON scalars unless stated otherwise. Numeric values and intermediate arithmetic are safe integers; integral JSON notations such as 1 and 1.0 denote the same number, while booleans are distinct. Strings contain Unicode scalar values without unpaired surrogates. Inputs have at most 48 events and eight simultaneous identities. Ordinary instances vary values; boundary instances emphasize empty/disabled/equality/no-op states; adversarial instances reorder callbacks and interleave edits; shift instances use longer traces/more identities within the same rules. These tasks test controller state/effects only, not visual quality, browser integration or screen-reader usability.

matchedCard.label: Archival provenance and original order
matchedCard.relation: The origin and original arrangement of records preserve relationships that can be lost when the same contents are rearranged arbitrarily. A later description or arrangement is distinct from evidence of the organization in which the records were produced.
assumptions: The origin or original order is known or supported by evidence.
Relationships among records contribute to their interpretation.
matchedCard.boundary: Original order can be lost or disrupted. A newly devised arrangement does not establish that it was the historical arrangement, and provenance does not make every recorded claim true.
matchedCard.source_fact: The National Archives explains provenance, preserving or restoring original order, and devising arrangements when necessary, emphasizing the evidential significance of context.

shuffledCard.label: Seed banking
shuffledCard.relation: Preserving a reserve and preserving its ability to reactivate are different conditions. Suitable material remains in controlled storage, while periodic sample recovery provides evidence of continued viability. Duplicate holdings reduce dependence on one location.
assumptions: The material tolerates the chosen storage treatment.
Samples provide relevant evidence about the collection they represent.
Duplicate collections remain identifiable as corresponding holdings.
shuffledCard.boundary: Some material cannot survive drying or freezing. Successful retention alone does not demonstrate viability, and sampled viability is not certainty about every stored item.
shuffledCard.source_fact: Kew stores suitable dried seeds in cold vaults, periodically tests germination, and commonly duplicates holdings in their country of origin. Some seeds do not tolerate conventional storage.

initial.explanation: Use the current ordered view as the sole range coordinate system. Disabled or absent clicks are no-ops; view updates filter selection and invalidate anchors. A shift click preserves a valid anchor, while a missing anchor is established at the clicked ID.
initial.mapping: config.options initializes view order and disabled status; state stores current options, selected IDs, and anchor; each event transforms those variables and emits sorted selected IDs plus anchor.
initial.assumptions: Inputs satisfy the stated schema and ID uniqueness constraints. JavaScript string ordering matches the required lexicographic ordering.

final.explanation: Maintains the current ordered view, selected IDs, and anchor in JSON state. View events replace the view, remove unavailable or disabled selections, and invalidate an unavailable anchor. Valid clicks apply plain, Ctrl, Shift, and Ctrl+Shift semantics using the current view; disabled or absent clicks are ignored. Outputs always sort selected IDs lexicographically while preserving the anchor.

initial.explanation: Maintain the current ordered option view, selected identity set, and anchor. Visibility edits prune invalid selections and anchors. Clicks apply plain, toggle, or range semantics; outputs are sorted lexicographically.
initial.mapping: The opaque state maps to {options, selected, anchor}; options preserve current view order, selected is an identity set represented as an array, and anchor is the range endpoint.
initial.assumptions: Events and option IDs satisfy the stated validity constraints. JavaScript string ordering matches the required lexicographic ordering.

initial.explanation: Maintain the current ordered view, selected IDs, and anchor. Views filter selection and invalidate unavailable anchors. Clicks use enabled IDs only; shift ranges follow the current view and skip disabled entries, while ctrl+shift unions.
initial.mapping: The optional rule maps ordered options to the current view, selected to retained identities, and anchor to the range-selection endpoint. The seed-banking analogy is not transferred because this task concerns interactive selection, not preservation or viability.
initial.assumptions: IDs are unique nonempty ASCII strings as specified. JavaScript string ordering is sufficient for the required lexicographic ID ordering.
